Treatment summary
Patient presented following a side-impact collision at an intersection with immediate
complaints of neck and low back pain. The mechanism of injury is consistent with the
reported symptoms, and the force of the impact is in keeping with soft tissue strain of
the cervical and lumbar regions. Over the course of care the patient attended 33
visits. Initial treatment focused on conservative management, including manual
therapy, stretching, and a home exericse program. Over time, additional services were
added in the following months, and visit frequency and the scope of care extended
beyond what is typically required for a strain of this kind. Examination findings
include reduced cervical range of motion and paraspinal tenderness, which support the
reported injury, while neurological screening and several orthopedic tests were within
normal limits. No prior injury or treatment to the neck or low back is known to this
provider. Billing records reviewed for this summray show no duplicate or repeated
charges. Prognosis is fair with continued home exercise and reassessment as needed.
